package-discovery.description: Every file the owner-route dispatcher reads when it scans the repository for packages: package manifests, direct package sources and the emoji-named entry files of each package, as observed by tracing a verify command and checked by the containment lane.

library-resources.description: Data files the repository library reads by computed path: its schemas and asset policies, and the taxonomy.

repository-sources.description: The sources a repository-wide scanner reads: every file of the source kinds, the schema JSON and the package manifests; not images, documents, fixture data or build output.

manifests.description: Every package manifest of the repository.

test-discovery.description: What test discovery reads: the taxonomy, feature files and the canonical emoji-named source of every language (the set the test domain's own discovery targets declare).

stdio-tree.description: The stdio plugin tree the ledger gates walk (STDIO_ROOT_REL) and the hub composition that consumes it.

rules.description: A root verify command that forwards to an owner target reads what the dispatcher scan reads and what that owner reads: its project, its crate closure and its script closure.
The package-purity, zero-touch and build-owners gates read the dispatcher scan and every package manifest (traced: 9.4k, 10.7k and 12.8k reads, all inside this set).
The artifact contract ownership law tests the owner crates of every artifact schema its fixture lists (generated from the fixture, checked by the rules test).
A verify gate that scans the repository reads the sources of every source kind.
A verify law reads the dispatcher scan, the TypeScript entries and Cargo crates its dispatcher branch names and the closure of those.
`lint repo` only reports completion of the lint graph that its dependsOn already ran.
`lint` runs dependency-cruiser over the four source roots with the lint boundary configuration.
The schema family reads the schema directories its sibling generate, docs and check targets already declare (schemaSources) and tests the schema crate.
Test discovery reads the taxonomy, feature files and the canonical emoji-named sources, as the test domain's own discovery targets declare.
The canvas test family runs the canvas module's native crate or React renderer tests.
The build library's own tests read the build library.
The stdio structural gates walk the stdio plugin tree (STDIO_ROOT_REL) through the artifact ledger.
The generate config check reads the repository's tool configuration manifests.
The entrypoint test runs one test file of the root command startup; it reads that test and its import closure, the library resources and the command's own script closure.
The semantic census reads every component of the repository by design: the census lists and compares all of them, so every file of every kind is an input.

These root commands re-enter the build tool (`repo run` or `run-many`) and their result is a function of the inputs of the targets they launch, which no static read of this command bounds; the owner decision is an uncached aggregate or explicit dependsOn.
The C++ custody and test-toolchain commands drive the CMake build library; their reads of the C++ trees and toolchain files are not yet traced, so they keep the inherited inputs.
The Storybook browser test reads every story and the components it imports; the story set is not yet derived from the Storybook configuration, so the inherited inputs stay.
Remaining root commands that scan or aggregate the repository read the source kinds, not the whole tree.
The hub typecheck reads exactly its tsconfig program: the include globs, the imports they reach and the package manifests resolution consults.
The plugin layer typecheck reads exactly the program of ✏️s/tsconfig.json.
The catalog publication reads plugin manifests, TypeScript and TOML sources of the plugin layer and the registry projection.
The stdio native checks compile the stdio crate and its path dependencies, which is what ^default stands for here.
The cross-plugin composition laws read their own directory and the closure of the tests they run.
The fixture placement laws walk all nine physical scopes of the repository (every top-level source tree) and compare every fixture path, so the whole tree is an input by design.
The stdio hub oracles read the hub stdio composition and the stdio plugin tree, and for the native cohorts the stdio crate closure.

The actor typegen exports through its Cargo exporter test, so it reads the crate, its test targets and the path-dependency closure its manifest names (never the TypeScript, CSS or other-product trees `^default` stands for), plus the command closure that the target lists itself; its own output (🤖️generated/🎭️actor/🟦️.ts) is written, not read.

The framework manifest generation exports through its Cargo exporter test, so it reads the crate, its test targets and the path-dependency closure its manifest names (never the TypeScript, CSS or other-product trees `^default` stands for), plus the command closure that the target lists itself; its own output (🛂️manifest/🤖️generated/🪪️manifest/🟦️.ts) is written, not read.

The UI contract generation runs the exporter test of the typegen crate its manifest names (`cargo test -p … --test typegen_export`), so it reads the contract crate, the typegen crate with its test targets and the path-dependency closure of both (never the TypeScript, CSS or other-product trees `^default` stands for), plus the command closure that the target lists itself; its own output (🛂️manifest/🤖️generated/📜️ui-contract/🟦️.ts) is written, not read.
